classification.difficultyReason: Transfer bearings onto the supplied diagram, justify the included angle and find the direct distance.

content.prompt:
A yacht sails from $X$ to $Y$ on a bearing of $130^\circ$ for 4.2 km.
It then turns and travels to $Z$ on a bearing of $025^\circ$ for 2.9 km.

spec.description: Source schematic: blue triangle, X upper left, Y lower right, Z above and slightly right of Y; XZ rises slightly right. Short black north arrows labelled N occur at all three vertices. No lengths or bearing values are supplied on the figure.
spec.mathematics: Vertex topology XYZ and three parallel north arrows. Source drawing is not to scale; numerical bearings and lengths remain in the stem.

answer.short: $XY=4.2\text{ km}$, $YZ=2.9\text{ km}$; bearings $130^\circ$ at $X$ and $025^\circ$ at $Y$.
answer.worked: $XY=4.2\text{ km}$ and $YZ=2.9\text{ km}$. Mark $130^\circ$ clockwise from north at $X$ to $XY$, and $025^\circ$ clockwise from north at $Y$ to $YZ$.

spec.description: Complete blue triangle with all three black north arrows, vertex labels, the two journey distances and clockwise bearing arcs at X and Y. Coordinates follow the stated bearings and lengths.
spec.mathematics: XY=4.2 km at bearing 130°; YZ=2.9 km at bearing 025°. XZ remains unlabelled.

answer.short: $\angle XYN=180^\circ-130^\circ=50^\circ$ by co-interior angles on parallel north lines; $\angle XYZ=50^\circ+25^\circ=75^\circ$.
answer.worked: The north lines are parallel, so co-interior angles give $\angle XYN=180^\circ-130^\circ=50^\circ$. Thus $\angle XYZ=50^\circ+25^\circ=75^\circ$.
